summary.oneLiner: Engineering margins remain pressured by delayed UP Jal Jeevan Mission execution and international project deferrals, while Roha chemical plant ramp-up is causing EBITDA compression; however, strong order inflows, budget tailwinds in solar/semiconductor/data centers, and long-term margin recovery from Roha create a turning point for FY27.

one-line thesis: Engineering margins remain pressured by delayed UP Jal Jeevan Mission execution and international project deferrals, while Roha chemical plant ramp-up is causing EBITDA compression; however, strong order inflows, budget tailwinds in solar/semiconductor/data centers, and long-term margin recovery from Roha create a turning point for FY27.
financial scorecard: revenue: +8% YoY (9M); EBITDA/margin: -9% YoY, 9.27% (9M) - impacted by Rs.169M exceptional gratuity provision and Roha depreciation; PAT (rptd): -12% YoY (9M), Rs.1,189M; PAT (normalized): +4% YoY (ex-gratuity provision); order book: Rs.28,330M (up from Rs.23,170M in Q2); net debt: Rs.345M term loan (Roha) + Rs.55M short-term, CWIP Rs.130M
guidance: revenue growth: FY27 to improve on FY26; margin: chemical margin to recover to ~28% long-term; order inflow: expect continued strength in solar/semiconductor/data centers; capex/commissioning: Roha CAPEX complete by Mar’26, full commissioning by FY27, 25% utilization targeted
order book & pipeline: Rs.28,330M total; includes Rs.2,050M solar contracts (2 wins), Rs.4,000M UP Jal Jeevan Mission backlog, international EPC projects deferred to Q4FY26
segment / subsidiary detail: Engineering: Q3 revenue flat YoY; EBIT down 28% due to UP project delays and international project deferrals; Chemicals: revenue +16% YoY; EBIT down 18% due to Roha depreciation, rupee depreciation, product mix; Consumer: revenue +28% YoY; loss widened to Rs.33M due to heavy A&P investment
growth verticals / optionality: Semiconductor ultra-pure water & ZLD; green hydrogen; data center water treatment; EU market expansion via acquisition; 200 legacy industrial clusters revival; critical mineral processing
margins & cost dynamics: Engineering: margin compression from low-margin UP projects and international mix shift; Chemicals: Roha depreciation (Rs.17M Q3), rupee-driven input cost inflation (pass-through underway); Consumer: negative margin due to strategic A&P spend
capex / expansion: Rs.450Cr total for Roha; Rs.285Cr capitalized, Rs.130Cr in CWIP; Rs.345Cr funded via term loan; Rs.105Cr via internal accruals
capital allocation: Prioritize debt reduction (Roha loan); reinvest Consumer segment profits into A&P; selective EPC project funding; no dividends mentioned
risks & watch-items: UP Jal Jeevan Mission fund delays; Roha ramp-up delays in certifications; semiconductor project profitability thresholds; rupee volatility; legacy project execution drag into FY27
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term pain but emphasizes structural improvements, selective bidding, and long-term tailwinds from budget and global trends; confident in Roha’s sustainability edge
non-obvious takeaways: Roha is a zero-liquid discharge plant with circular design — 1/3 CAPEX dedicated to sustainability, making it a global benchmark; this justifies longer payback (4-5 yrs) and is a strategic moat

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Company snapshot claims "62 + YEARS OF EXPERTISE", operations in 50+ countries, "ONE OF ASIA'S LARGEST SERVICE NETWORKS" and 200,000+ installations world-wide with 3,000+ core industry projects.
- Describes itself as "Leaders in Resins, Membranes & Chemicals, with a Unique End-to-End Portfolio Spanning Solutions, Digital & Services", serving industries, institutions, homes and communities.
- Coverage spans the full water chain — source water and pretreatment, process water, high purity and ultra pure water, industrial wastewater treatment, recycle and Zero Liquid Discharge, drinking water, and municipal and sewage treatment including tertiary recycle and sludge management.
- International revenue share stated at 30%, with global assembly hubs in UAE, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Indonesia and Bangladesh and "EXPORTS ACROSS CONTINENTS".
- Capability set listed as Resins, Membranes, Chemicals, Solutions, Services and Digital.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Segment reporting change] The deck shows a move from Current Reporting (Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products, Lifecycle Services, Specialty Chemicals, Consumer Products) to New Reporting segments: Institutional, Engineering, Chemicals and Consumer Products.
- [Order book] As on 30 June 2026, for Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services: Total Orderbook ~INR 24,730 Mn, of which Engineering projects ~INR 21,820 Mn, Outstanding Sri Lanka ~INR 100 Mn and Outstanding UP SWSM ~INR 2,810 Mn; Bid Pipeline ~INR 97,770 Mn. Engineering projects are stated as excluding the Sri Lanka order, UP SWSM and the recent contract awarded to the company.
- [New contract] A recent contract awarded to the company of USD 52.83 Mn by Hyundai Engineering & Construction is explicitly excluded from the quoted engineering order book.
- [Margin overhang] Recurring structural drags named across slides: "Impact of Higher Cost profile in certain EPC contracts", "Margins continue to be impacted by legacy projects", "Slowed execution of UP Contract", "Impact of West Asia crisis" and "Investment in overseas Geographies".
- [Shareholding, 30 June 2026] Promoter 25.4%, Employee Trust 16.2%, Mutual Funds 12.5%, Foreign Portfolio Investors 4.9%, Alternative Investment Funds 2.8%, Others 38.2%; EPS is stated to include the impact of 2,37,36,140 shares held by IEI/HMIL Shareholding (Staff Welfare) Trusts and 43,78,740 shares held by subsidiaries.
